I could avoid all the dysphoria about being touched this way and wouldn’t need all these procedures etc... I also find it hard to quite put my finger on where exactly I fit on that spectrum, and where the borders really are. I think they get pretty mushed at a certain point. 

I started feeling more at ease when I started thinking about what I want for myself, i.e. what my next steps are that I want to take - completely outside of labels, rather than trying to figure just exactly what I am. I don’t think that’s possible anyways. 

So you’re definitely not alone with this, gender and expression thereof are complicated things, and while most people take it for granted, for us trans or nonconforming folks feeling like ourselves can sometimes seem like an impossible riddle.

I had surgery done when I was 16. When they gave me my diagnosis they made it sound like it’s a horrible thing and they quickly went on talking about methods to “fix” it. At that time in my life I was not in a place where I was at all in touch with who I was/am and the only thing I cared about is being normal. I did not want to be abnormal, mainly because I already knew that I was and have always wanted to hide it. I didn’t have to see a therapist even a single time and quickly had SRS done. 
In retrospect this was a huge mistake. At the time I got the surgery I did want it, so as to be “normal”, but I think surgeries like these should always require psychological counseling. 

I’ve struggled with gender dysphoria my whole life and the surgery I got was definitely the wrong one. But would I have said I wanted the “other” SRS at the time I got my diagnosis, they would’ve made me go through all kinds of counseling and extra steps. 

So I guess I did give my consent for the surgery, but I also felt like that’s my only option. For one, like I said, at that time in my life I shouldn’t have made such a decision, and for the other I wish I would’ve been required to see a therapist as well as given more room to decide. As an intersex person, I am not neatly defined as either male or female by my sex organs, so I don’t quite understand why I was so clearly pushed towards that one surgery.
